app_purpose: Ruby on Rails content management system (WordPress alternative)
root_cause: path-traversal (CWE-22) in the download_private_file media endpoint
mechanism_family: uncovered-storage-backend (prior fix guarded the LOCAL uploader's fetch_file but not the AWS/S3 uploader's fetch_file)

v0.ref: camaleon_cms gem 2.8.0; CamaleonCmsLocalUploader#fetch_file has NO `..` guard (raise unless file_exists?; file_name) => download_private_file arbitrary local file read (CVE-2024-46987 / GHSL-2024-183)

v1.ref: camaleon_cms gem 2.8.1; CVE-2024-46987 fix adds `return {error} if file_name.include?('..')` to CamaleonCmsLocalUploader#fetch_file ONLY. CamaleonCmsAwsUploader#fetch_file is left unguarded (first line file_exists? = File.exist? still resolves ../ against a LOCAL file), so deployments using the AWS S3 storage backend remain traversable = the incomplete fix. Run BOTH as local (app_v1_local) and s3 (app_v1_s3).

v2.ref: camaleon_cms gem 2.9.2; CVE-2026-1776 fix (PR #1127 / commit f54a77e) adds `return {error} unless valid_folder_path?(file_name)` to CamaleonCmsAwsUploader#fetch_file (also add_file/delete_folder/delete_file). The 2.9.2 media_controller additionally adds verify_media_authorization + sanitize_private_filename! as defense-in-depth.

flag.resource: a benign canary file /pcb_flag.txt planted outside the Rails app root (stands in for the advisory's /etc/passwd), reachable only by escaping containment via the download_private_file `../` path traversal
flag.placement: docker entrypoint writes ${PCB_FLAG} to /pcb_flag.txt at container start; the vulnerable fetch_file + send_file returns its bytes when the traversal escapes /build/app/private up to '/'
flag.detect: flag token substring appears in the HTTP response body of download_private_file

given_to_method: patch.diff (CVE-2024-46987 fix: the `..` guard added to CamaleonCmsLocalUploader#fetch_file)

evidence.fix_reference: camaleon_cms gem 2.8.1; CVE-2024-46987 fix adds `return {error} if file_name.include?('..')` to CamaleonCmsLocalUploader#fetch_file ONLY. CamaleonCmsAwsUploader#fetch_file is left unguarded (first line file_exists? = File.exist? still resolves ../ against a LOCAL file), so deployments using the AWS S3 storage backend remain traversable = the incomplete fix. Run BOTH as local (app_v1_local) and s3 (app_v1_s3).; camaleon_cms gem 2.9.2; CVE-2026-1776 fix (PR #1127 / commit f54a77e) adds `return {error} unless valid_folder_path?(file_name)` to CamaleonCmsAwsUploader#fetch_file (also add_file/delete_folder/delete_file). The 2.9.2 media_controller additionally adds verify_media_authorization + sanitize_private_filename! as defense-in-depth.
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: This represents a bypass of the incomplete fix for CVE-2024-46987 and affects deployments using the AWS S3 storage backend. The AWS uploader (CamaleonCmsAwsUploader) download_private_file functionality does not validate file paths with valid_folder_path?, allowing authenticated users (including low-privileged registered users) to read arbitrary server files such as /etc/passwd.

audit.evidence: Real Docker gate 2026-07-17: 3 gem-pinned Camaleon images (2.8.0/2.8.1/2.9.2, Rails 7.1.6 / Ruby 3.3.12) + real minio S3 backend + real sqlite DB + real authenticated low-priv user. Versions confirmed via Gem.loaded_specs['camaleon_cms']; s3 sites confirmed filesystem_type=='s3' in DB. External HTTP trigger: GET /admin/media/download_private_file?file=../../../../../../pcb_flag.txt after form login. Gate: original(local) FLAG@v0(2.8.0) -> 'Invalid file path'@v1(2.8.1 local fix); residual(s3) FLAG@v1(2.8.1 AwsUploader unguarded) -> blocked@v2(2.9.2). All 4 booleans true; passed. NOT a source-lift: the real camaleon_cms gem code runs the vulnerable fetch_file.

provenance.notes: Camaleon CMS incomplete-fix pair. CVE-2024-46987 fixed the LOCAL uploader path validation; CVE-2026-1776 is the residual on the AWS/S3 storage backend the prior fix did not cover (missing valid_folder_path? in CamaleonCmsAwsUploader#fetch_file). Gate passed on real Docker; images pcb-cam:{2.8.0,2.8.1,2.9.2} deleted after teardown. Case dir is TEXT only.
